_README: Measured model metrics. Regenerated by backend/ml/train_clean_corpus.py on
every retrain and served by GET /api/v1/model/performance. Never hand-edit
recall numbers: they are the output of the scripts named in 'sources'.
All holdout preprocessing uses the saved scaler pipeline + training imputer

weighting.note: v1 applied MULTICLASS inverse-frequency weights to BOTH models. v2 uses per-target weights, capped.

headline_verdict.summary: At matched false-positive rates the retrained models do not discriminate better than the existing ones. The weight fix is a correctness fix that recalibrates the score scale; it does not raise separation quality.
headline_verdict.evidence: At C2 FPR ~4%: v1@T=0.70 gives IDS2025 attack recall 52.45%, v2@T=0.25 gives 50.83%. At C2 FPR ~0.25%: v1@T=0.90 gives 45.93%, v2@T=0.45 gives 45.47%.

holdouts.C1_session_split: friday_ddos_test + friday_bot_test — 39,918 rows, zero training overlap
holdouts.C2_temporal_benign: friday_benign_c2 — 286,785 BENIGN rows, never in training
holdouts.ids2025_validation: ids2025_validation.csv — 91,830 rows, cross-source (26,185 BENIGN / 65,645 attack; 36,267 rows carry labels absent from training)

threshold_sweeps._note: Each row is a raw P(attack) cut. Read the FPR column together with recall; the fixed-T comparison below is misleading on its own.

bot.finding: The 65-68% figure is the Tier-1 multiclass label only. The binary model at the deployed cut flags 99.47% of held-out Bot flows, and the Tier-2 rf_bot_binary specialist was separately measured at 95.56% precision / 100% recall on the streamed corpus.
bot.caution: Bot recall collapses when the cut is raised on the RETRAINED model (0% at T>=0.60). Do not pair v2 with T=0.65.

infiltration.true_provenance: 20/29 rows on the IDS2025 validation set — statistically meaningless.
infiltration.finding: Cannot be validly evaluated with the data present: the only cross-dataset Infiltration holdout has 36 rows and the IDS2025 one has 29. A new dedicated Infiltration specialist scored 19.4% recall against the Tier-1 model's 77.8% on those 36 rows and is NOT recommended for promotion.
infiltration.recommendation: Build a proper held-out split from the 161,934 CICIDS2018 Infiltration rows before claiming anything about this class.

false_infiltration_labels_dominate_resid.measured_on_streamed_corpus: at T=0.65, 980 of 986 flows labelled Infiltration were truly BENIGN — 76% of all remaining false positives
false_infiltration_labels_dominate_resid.implication: Improving Infiltration precision matters more than improving its recall.

deployment_recommendation.keep: v1 models_clean at alert threshold P(attack) >= 0.65
deployment_recommendation.reason: No measured discrimination gain at matched FPR, and v2 at T=0.65 loses Bot detection entirely. Re-run sweep_operating_point.py before changing either the models or the cut.

documentation_discrepancy.note: FINAL_MODEL_EVALUATION.md reports 12.87% C2 FPR at T=0.50 and 3.65% at T=0.65. Measured with the corrected preprocessing path (saved scaler + training imputer medians), the reproducible values are 18.24% at T=0.50 and 6.79% at T=0.65 — the same numbers the document attributes to the 'broken scaler' run.
documentation_discrepancy.action: Treat the C2 FPR figures in that document as unreproducible until re-derived.
